rules_text:
Rules summary For tips on how to play Kingdom Builder, see Tips_KingdomBuilder Contents 1 Game Layout 1.1 Terrain spaces 1.2 Location spaces 1.3 Scoring cards 2 Placing Settlements 3 Location Tiles 3.1 Extra action: Build one additional settlement from your personal supply 3.2 Extra action: Move one of your existing settlements 4 Game End Game Layout Kingdom Builder comes with eight different playing boards (called Sectors ). The game starts with four random sector boards and three random scoring cards. Each of the four sector boards is comprised of 100 hexes in a unique combination of Terrain hexes, Castle hexes and Location hexes. Each player starts with forty settlements (houses) in their supply and is dealt one one Terrain Card from the Terrain Deck. Terrain spaces There are five terrain types on which you are allowed to build a settlement: Grass, Canyon, Desert, Flower and Forest. There are two terrain types on which you are not allowed to build a settlement: Water and Mountains. Location spaces Each sector board contains one or two Castles . Placing a settlement next to a Castle hex will reward you with 3 victory points at the end of the game. Each sector board contains one or two Locations . Placing a settlement next to a Location hex will earn you a Location Tile which provides an extra action during the remainder of your future turns. Like Water and Mountains, you are not allowed to build a settlement on Castle or Location hexes. Scoring cards The three random scoring cards define how players will earn gold (victory points) in the game, such as earning gold for your settlements built next to water hexes or having the majority of settlements in a sector of the board, etc. A fourth scoring card ( Castle ) is present in every game and allows players to earn gold by building next to Castles. Placing Settlements Each turn you must place three of your settlements on the terrain type shown on your terrain card, with the following considerations: 1) If possible you must build adjacent to your existing settlements. Never forget this, managing adjacency is the key to the game. 2) Placing a settlement next to a Location hex will grant you its corresponding tile that you will be able to activate in every future turn. Note: Location Tiles are limited in quantity. Two Location Tiles are placed on each Location hex and are claimed on a "first come, first take" basis. You can only earn one location tile per specific location hex. Location Tiles Location Tiles allow you to activate extra actions. Each tile's action can be used once per turn starting on the turn after you obtain the tile. These extra actions can be used either before or after your mandatory "build three settlements" action, but not in the midst of your "build three" action. The player keeps a location tile as long as at least one of their settlements is adjacent to the corresponding location. If ever they move their last settlement away from such a location (e.g., by using the action of Barn, Harbor or Paddock), they forfeit that tile and it is removed from the game. After losing a tile from a location, a player cannot re-obtain the tile from that same location hex. Losing a location tile happens immediately when you no longer are adjacent to the location hex. Extra action: Build one additional settlement from your personal supply Location Name/ Sector Board Tile Front Action Summary Qty. of Location Hexes on Board Qty. of Castle Hexes on Board Action Description Oracle 1 Location hex (2 Location Tiles) 2 Castles Build one settlement on a hex of the same type as your played Terrain Card. Build adjacent if possible. Farm 2 Location hexes (4 Location Tiles) 1 Castle Build one settlement on Grass. Build adjacent if possible. Oasis 2 Location hexes (4 Location Tiles) 1 Castle Build one settlement on a Desert hex. Build adjacent if possible. Tower 2 Location hexes (4 Location Tiles) 1 Castle Build one settlement at the edge on the board. Choose any of the 5 suitable terrain type hexes. Build adjacent if possible. Tavern 2 Location hexes (4 Location Tiles) 1 Castle Build one settlement at the end of a string of at least 3 of your own settlements. The orientation of the string does not matter (horizontally or diagonally). The chosen hex must be suitable for building. Extra action: Move one of your existing settlements Location Name/ Sector Board Tile Front Action Summary Qty. of Location Hexes on Board Qty. of Castle Hexes on Board Action Description Harbor 1 Location hex (2 Location Tiles) 2 Castles Move any one of your existing settlements to a water hex. (This is the only way to build settlements on water hexes.) Build adjacent if possible. Barn 2 Location hexes (4 Location Tiles) 1 Castle Move any one of your existing settlements to a hex of the same type as your played Terrain Card. Build adjacent if possible. Paddock 2 Location hexes (4 Location Tiles) 1 Castle Move any one of your existing settlements two hexes in a straight line in any direction to an eligible hex. You may jump across any terrain type hex, even mountain, water, castle, location and/or your own and other players' settlement. The target hex does not have be adjacent to one of your existing settlements. Game End The game ends at the end of the round in which one player has built the last settlement from their personal supply. Each player scores according to the three scoring cards, plus 3 gold for each castle hex they have a settlement next to.

community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] After one play I can already see that there is absolutely nothing in this game that would make me want to play it again. No choices, empty decisions and lots and lots of luck... Worst game I played in Essen'11.

[Rating: 1/10] Borring and poor. Some cards have a big unbalance, with one of the cards the diference between the person who gained more points and the person who gained less was only 2 points. Trying to collect points of this card was completly a waste of time.  Anyway people who never played boardgames or play from time to time maybe have a good time playing.  The best for me was how much we laught talking about the "flower territory"

[Rating: 1/10] Massive strategical depth in perfect combination with swift but highly engaging gameplay keep me coming back to this unfortunately often-overlooked gem for more. Beautiful components and a scoring system that makes each game a totally unique experience magnificently complete this really neat package. Includes nuclear tanks.

[Rating: 1/10] This is a game sorely in need of a comeback mechanism. Too scoring and power combinations result in setups where the first player to get a particular power gets the rest of the powers and nobody else can catch up, but the game continues for many turns after such a tipping point has been reached.

[Rating: 1/10] I fail to understand why anyone likes this game. It's boring, there's no theme, it's entirely random due to the card deck and some of the winning conditions are just plain broken. This will easily go on my Top 10 Worst Games.

[Rating: 1/10] Love this game will only play with the one special tile house rule though. makes game a lot more interesting  So why 1 star: Because a year on from when it was due to be delivered I'm still waiting for my expansion from queen. The experience has definitely tempered my enjoyment of the game. It's hard to  even look at the box without experiencing extreme anger.  Traded in for big box.

[Rating: 1/10] Kingdom Builder just felt like a soulless point salad with player boards.  Neither play with different groups of players did anything for any of us.

[Rating: 1/10] Played a few times, why would you play game where the game tells you where to play?    Not for me.

[Rating: 1/10] Well I would rather play Paris Connection ten out of ten times.  This game is fine but it's not useful for me.  Territory control game that kind of feels like the scoring phase of Fjords expanded into a whole game.  The strategy is more about reacting to the map and shedding cubes than the investments of Paris Connection so the comparison isn't entirely fair, but they occupy for me the same light euro niche.

[Rating: 1/10] I used to enjoy it, but I can't stand looking at it after how Queen Games treated us on Kickstarter for the expansions.
